title: Timed Mixed Lab Set B

header.html: All five domains (weighted like the exam: Environment, Configuration and Security 4 tasks, Application Design and Build 3, Application Deployment 3, Services and Networking 3, Observability and Maintenance 3)
review of every domain under time pressure
Kubernetes v1.37.0; every task in this set was executed and validated in Modules 1 to 16 (setup, failing check, solution, passing check, wrong answers rejected)

html:
1How to use this set

  1. Reset: make sure the lab cluster is healthy (kubectl get nodes shows three Ready nodes).
  2. Start a 120-minute timer. Allowed documentation only: kubernetes.io/docs and blog, helm.sh/docs.
  3. For each task, prepare its starting state with python run_labs.py --setup <lab-id> (it also prints the task), then solve it as you would on the exam.
  4. Score yourself with python run_labs.py --check <lab-id>. A task is all-or-nothing, like the exam's scoring.
  5. Pass mark: 66% of the points.

Honest note: this set reuses tasks from the module labs, so you have seen their wording before. Use it as a timed rehearsal of speed and routine, then use the killer.sh simulator for tasks you have never seen.

2Tasks

Set size: 16 tasks, 107 points in total. Pass mark: 66%, which is 71 points. Suggested time: 120 minutes (the labs' own time estimates add up to 116 minutes). Do the tasks in order, flag what you skip, and check your work as you would on the exam.

Task 1 (Environment, 6 points, about 7 minutes) m09-02-secret-env-file

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace sec, create a Secret db-creds with username=admin and password=S3cret!. Create a Pod dbclient (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that gets the environment variable DB_USER from the Secret key username and mounts the whole Secret read-only at /etc/db.

Task 2 (Environment, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m10-02-oomkilled-limit

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace res, the Pod of the Deployment hog is repeatedly killed because it uses more memory than its limit (OOMKilled). Without changing the image or the command, set the memory limit of its container to 256Mi and its memory request to 64Mi, and wait until the Deployment has 1 Ready replica that keeps running.

Task 3 (Environment, 8 points, about 9 minutes) m11-06-fix-forbidden-api-call

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace auth, the Pod caller (ServiceAccount app-sa) asks the API server every 3 seconds for the list of Pods in its own namespace and prints the HTTP status code. It prints 403. Without changing the Pod, give its ServiceAccount exactly the access it needs, namely list on Pods in the namespace auth (use a Role named pod-lister and a RoleBinding named pod-lister-binding), so that the log shows 200.

Task 4 (Environment, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m13-03-fix-custom-resource

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The CRD for the kind Widget (group shop.example.com) is installed. The manifest ~/work/widget.yaml for the Widget blue-one in the namespace crd is rejected by the API server. Read the error, fix the manifest without changing the name, and create the object. It must end up with spec.size: 3 and spec.color: blue.

Task 5 (Design and Build, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m02-04-cronjob-settings

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace wl, create a CronJob named tick with the image busybox:1.36 that runs date every 5 minutes. It must not start a run while the previous one is still running (concurrencyPolicy: Forbid), and keep the last 2 successful and the last 1 failed Jobs. Then start one run now, by creating a Job named tick-manual from the CronJob, and wait until that Job is complete.

Task 6 (Design and Build, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m03-05-native-sidecar-job

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace mc, the Job report never completes, because its Pod has a second container tail (a log helper that sleeps forever) next to the main container main. Keep the tail container, but change the Job so that it completes: declare tail as a native sidecar (an init container with restartPolicy: Always). The manifest is in ~/work/report-job.yaml. A Job's Pod template cannot be edited, so delete the Job and create it again from the corrected file; wait until the Job is complete.

Task 7 (Design and Build, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m04-04-dynamic-pvc-persists

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace vol, create a PersistentVolumeClaim named data that requests 1Gi with ReadWriteOnce from the cluster's default StorageClass (do not name a class). Create a Pod writer (image busybox:1.36) that mounts it at /data and runs sh -c "echo kept-after-delete > /data/note.txt; sleep 3600". When the file exists, delete the Pod writer and create a Pod reader (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that mounts the same claim at /data. The file must still be there.

Task 8 (Deployment, 7 points, about 7 minutes) m05-04-blue-green-switch

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace bg, a blue version (Deployment app-blue) and a green version (Deployment app-green) of an application are both running. The Service shop currently sends all traffic to the blue version. Switch the live traffic to the green version by changing the Service, and leave both Deployments running (so that you can switch back).

Task 9 (Deployment, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m06-03-helm-values-file

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The file ~/work/prod-values.yaml holds the settings for production. Install the newest version of the chart local/webapp (the repository local is already added) as the release site in the namespace helm-ns (create it with the install), taking the values from that file. Do not edit the file.

Task 10 (Deployment, 8 points, about 9 minutes) m06-07-kustomize-config-generator

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

A Kustomize base exists in ~/kust/base (a Deployment web and a Service web). Create an overlay in ~/kust/overlays/staging that reuses the base and: sets the namespace staging, generates a ConfigMap named web-config with the literal LEVEL=info, and patches the Deployment so that its container loads all keys of that ConfigMap as environment variables (envFrom). Do not edit the base. Create the namespace staging and apply the overlay. The running Pod must show LEVEL=info in its environment.

Task 11 (Networking, 5 points, about 5 minutes) m14-02-nodeport-service

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace svc2, expose the Deployment web (nginx on port 80) with a Service named web-np of type NodePort, service port 80, using the fixed node port 30080.

Task 12 (Networking, 8 points, about 9 minutes) m15-03-ingress-tls

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace ing2, the Service a exists. A certificate and key for secure.example.com are in ~/answers/tls.crt and ~/answers/tls.key. Create a TLS Secret named web-tls from them, and an Ingress named secure (class traefik) that serves the host secure.example.com from the Service a on port 80 and uses the Secret for HTTPS.

Task 13 (Networking, 8 points, about 9 minutes) m16-03-egress-policy

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace np3, the Pod app (busybox) must only be allowed to send traffic to (a) Pods labelled app=db on TCP port 80 and (b) the cluster DNS on port 53 (UDP and TCP). All other outgoing traffic from app must be blocked. Create one NetworkPolicy named app-egress for the Pod app.

Task 14 (Observability, 7 points, about 8 minutes) m07-03-startup-probe

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The Pod slow in the namespace probes (manifest ~/work/slow.yaml) needs about 25 seconds to start, but its liveness probe starts checking after 1 second and keeps killing it. Without removing or loosening the liveness probe, add a startup probe to the container that runs the same command test -f /tmp/started every 5 seconds with failureThreshold: 12, so that the liveness probe only begins after the app has started. Recreate the Pod from the corrected manifest. It must become Ready with restartCount 0.

Task 15 (Observability, 6 points, about 6 minutes) m08-07-missing-configmap

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace dbg, the Pod of the Deployment svc does not start (CreateContainerConfigError). Find the cause with kubectl describe, and fix it without changing the Deployment: create what is missing so that the Deployment has 1 Ready replica. The application expects LEVEL=info from that source.

Task 16 (Observability, 5 points, about 5 minutes) m08-01-logs-one-container

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The Pod shop in the namespace dbg has two containers, web and worker. Write only the last 3 lines of the log of the container worker to ~/answers/worker-tail.txt on the host where you run kubectl.

<!-- /SET -->

3Reference solutions

Open these only after the timer ends.

Solution 1: m09-02-secret-env-file

kubectl -n sec create secret generic db-creds --from-literal=username=admin --from-literal='password=S3cret!'
kubectl -n sec apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: dbclient}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    env:
    - name: DB_USER
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef: {name: db-creds, key: username}
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: creds, mountPath: /etc/db, readOnly: true}
  volumes:
  - name: creds
    secret: {secretName: db-creds}
Y
kubectl -n sec wait --for=condition=Ready pod/dbclient --timeout=120s
kubectl -n sec exec dbclient -- sh -c 'echo $DB_USER; cat /etc/db/password'

Solution 2: m10-02-oomkilled-limit

kubectl -n res describe pod -l app=hog | grep -iE "OOMKilled|Reason|Limits|memory"
kubectl -n res set resources deployment hog --requests=memory=64Mi --limits=memory=256Mi
kubectl -n res rollout status deployment hog --timeout=120s

Solution 3: m11-06-fix-forbidden-api-call

kubectl -n auth logs caller | tail -2
kubectl -n auth create role pod-lister --verb=list --resource=pods
kubectl -n auth create rolebinding pod-lister-binding --role=pod-lister --serviceaccount=auth:app-sa
sleep 6
kubectl -n auth logs caller | tail -2

Solution 4: m13-03-fix-custom-resource

kubectl apply -f ~/work/widget.yaml 2>&1 | head -5
kubectl explain widget.spec
sed -i 's/size: "three"/size: 3/; s/color: navy/color: blue/' ~/work/widget.yaml
kubectl apply -f ~/work/widget.yaml
kubectl -n crd get widgets

Solution 5: m02-04-cronjob-settings

kubectl -n wl create cronjob tick --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule="*/5 * * * *" -- date
kubectl -n wl patch cronjob tick -p '{"spec":{"concurrencyPolicy":"Forbid","successfulJobsHistoryLimit":2,"failedJobsHistoryLimit":1}}'
kubectl -n wl create job tick-manual --from=cronjob/tick
kubectl -n wl wait --for=condition=complete job/tick-manual --timeout=180s

Solution 6: m03-05-native-sidecar-job

kubectl -n mc delete job report --wait=true
cat > ~/work/report-job.yaml <<'Y'
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: report
  namespace: mc
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      initContainers:
      - name: tail
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep", "3600"]
        restartPolicy: Always
      containers:
      - name: main
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo report finished"]
Y
kubectl apply -f ~/work/report-job.yaml
kubectl -n mc wait --for=condition=complete job/report --timeout=180s

Solution 7: m04-04-dynamic-pvc-persists

kubectl -n vol apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: writer
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo kept-after-delete > /data/note.txt; sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: store, mountPath: /data}
  volumes:
  - name: store
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: data
Y
kubectl -n vol wait --for=condition=Ready pod/writer --timeout=180s
sleep 3
kubectl -n vol delete pod writer --wait=true
kubectl -n vol apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: reader
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: store, mountPath: /data}
  volumes:
  - name: store
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: data
Y
kubectl -n vol wait --for=condition=Ready pod/reader --timeout=180s
kubectl -n vol exec reader -- cat /data/note.txt

Solution 8: m05-04-blue-green-switch

kubectl -n bg get svc shop -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'; echo
kubectl -n bg patch service shop -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app":"shop","version":"green"}}}'
kubectl -n bg get endpoints shop

Solution 9: m06-03-helm-values-file

helm show values local/webapp | head -20
helm install site local/webapp -n helm-ns --create-namespace -f ~/work/prod-values.yaml --wait --timeout 120s
helm get values site -n helm-ns

Solution 10: m06-07-kustomize-config-generator

cat > ~/kust/overlays/staging/kustomization.yaml <<'Y'
resources:
- ../../base
namespace: staging
configMapGenerator:
- name: web-config
  literals:
  - LEVEL=info
patches:
- target: {kind: Deployment, name: web}
  patch: |-
    - op: add
      path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/envFrom
      value:
      - configMapRef:
          name: web-config
Y
kubectl kustomize ~/kust/overlays/staging | head -40
kubectl create ns staging
kubectl apply -k ~/kust/overlays/staging
kubectl -n staging rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s
kubectl -n staging exec deploy/web -- printenv LEVEL

Solution 11: m14-02-nodeport-service

kubectl -n svc2 expose deployment web --name=web-np --port=80 --type=NodePort --dry-run=client -o yaml > /tmp/web-np.yaml
sed -i 's/  - port: 80/  - port: 80\n    nodePort: 30080/' /tmp/web-np.yaml
kubectl -n svc2 apply -f /tmp/web-np.yaml
kubectl -n svc2 get svc web-np

Solution 12: m15-03-ingress-tls

kubectl -n ing2 create secret tls web-tls --cert=$HOME/answers/tls.crt --key=$HOME/answers/tls.key
kubectl -n ing2 create ingress secure --class=traefik --rule="secure.example.com/*=a:80,tls=web-tls"
kubectl -n ing2 get ingress secure
sleep 5

Solution 13: m16-03-egress-policy

kubectl -n np3 apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: app-egress}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: app}}
  policyTypes: [Egress]
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: db}}
    ports:
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 80}
  - ports:
    - {protocol: UDP, port: 53}
    - {protocol: TCP, port: 53}
Y
sleep 5

Solution 14: m07-03-startup-probe

kubectl -n probes delete pod slow --wait=true
cat > ~/work/slow.yaml <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: slow
  namespace: probes
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 25; touch /tmp/started; sleep 3600"]
    startupProbe:
      exec:
        command: ["sh", "-c", "test -f /tmp/started"]
      periodSeconds: 5
      failureThreshold: 12
    livenessProbe:
      exec:
        command: ["sh", "-c", "test -f /tmp/started"]
      initialDelaySeconds: 1
      periodSeconds: 2
      failureThreshold: 2
Y
kubectl apply -f ~/work/slow.yaml
kubectl -n probes wait --for=condition=Ready pod/slow --timeout=120s
kubectl -n probes get pod slow

Solution 15: m08-07-missing-configmap

kubectl -n dbg describe pod -l app=svc | grep -i -A3 "Events"
kubectl -n dbg create configmap app-config --from-literal=LEVEL=info
kubectl -n dbg rollout status deployment svc --timeout=120s

Solution 16: m08-01-logs-one-container

kubectl -n dbg logs shop -c worker --tail=3 > ~/answers/worker-tail.txt
cat ~/answers/worker-tail.txt

4Review after the set

  • Count your points per domain and compare them with the pass mark of 66 percent.
  • Write every reading mistake (wrong namespace, wrong name, missing context line) on your personal checklist.
  • Redo the tasks you flagged or failed, this time with the reference solution closed.
  • Compare your domain scores with Set A and redo the three slowest tasks.

5Recall questions

R1How many points do you need to pass the set, and what is the passing score of the exam?

Show the answer

66% of the points, the same as the exam.

R2What is the first action on every task?

Show the answer

Run the context line and note the exact names and namespaces.

R3What do you do with a task that is stuck after about six minutes?

Show the answer

Flag it, move on and return at the end.

R4Which command shows why a Pod is Pending or crashing?

Show the answer

kubectl describe pod, then kubectl logs (--previous after a restart).

R5Which two flags generate YAML without creating the object?

Show the answer

--dry-run=client -o yaml.

R6How do you confirm that a Service has working backends?

Show the answer

kubectl get endpoints <service> and a test request from a throw-away Pod.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Time 120 minutes, about 6 to 8 minutes per task
Pass 66% of the points; tasks are all-or-nothing
Order easy first, flag the hard ones, keep time to verify
Verify a second command (get, describe, logs, a test request)
After the set repeat the tasks you flagged, then the other set
